lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty — and darkness was over the surface of the deep.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Let there be light.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And God saw that the light was good. He separated the light from the darkness — calling the light 'Day' and the darkness 'Night.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now watch the days unfold. Place each part of the world in the order God spoke it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the second day, God formed the sky — a vault between the waters above and the waters below. And it was so.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the third day, the waters gathered. Dry ground appeared. And every seed-bearing plant and tree with fruit burst forth across the earth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the fourth day, God set the sun, moon, and stars in the vault to govern day and night.

choices.label: Admire the vastness ✨
choices.note: The cosmos stretches beyond counting — each star named by Him.

choices.label: Wonder at their purpose 🔭
choices.note: Lights to mark seasons, days, and years. Order from chaos.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the fifth day, the waters teemed with living creatures, and birds filled the sky. On the sixth, the land animals.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then God said, 'Let us make mankind in our image, to rule over every living creature.' And it was so.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Let us make mankind in our image, to have dominion —

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Male and female, in our image, we create them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Lord God formed a man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life. And the man became a living being.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: I have placed him in the garden to work it and keep it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The garden was a paradise — every tree was pleasing to the eye, and every fruit was good for food. The tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil stood in its midst.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: You may eat from any tree. But from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil — you must not eat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For on the day that you eat from it, you will surely die.

choices.label: Why this one tree? 🤔
choices.note: A fair question. Some boundaries exist not to withhold, but to protect.

choices.label: Trust without question ✅
choices.note: Obedience is its own reward when the giver is love.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the man tended the garden. He named every creature. And he walked with God in the cool of the day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Lord God said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: God brought every creature to Adam to see what he would name them. But among all the beasts, birds, and fish...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ...no suitable helper was found for Adam.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall on the man. While he slept, God took one of his ribs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the Lord built a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man. Then He brought her to the man.

lines.speaker: adam
lines.text: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh! She shall be called 'woman' — for she was taken out of man.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man shall leave his father and mother and be united to his wife. And the two shall become one flesh.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Thus the garden held its first couple — naked in innocence, walking in peace.

lines.speaker: serpent
lines.text: Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?

lines.speaker: eve
lines.text: We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden. But as for the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of the garden...

lines.speaker: serpent
lines.text: You will not certainly die. For God knows that when you eat from it, your eyes will be opened — and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.

lines.speaker: eve
lines.text: Are you sure? He said we would die if we eat. But you say we will be like God...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fruit was good for food and pleasing to the eye. It promised wisdom — the one thing God had withheld.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She looked at the fruit, longing for what it promised. Then she took some and ate it.

choices.label: Resist the serpent 🛡️
choices.note: The moment passes. Temptation without action is just a whisper.

choices.label: Taste the fruit 🍎
choices.note: The first bite changes everything. Knowledge comes at the price of innocence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She gave some to her husband, who was with her. And he ate it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The moment the fruit touched their lips, something tore. Shame flooded in. Their eyes were opened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They heard God approaching. And they hid — from each other, and from Him.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Adam, where are you?

lines.speaker: adam
lines.text: I heard You in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked. So I hid.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: God spoke to the serpent, and pronounced judgment on the curse of the earth.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Because you have listened to your wife and eaten... the ground is cursed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He made garments of skin for them — covering their nakedness with His own hands.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the Lord God said, 'Now the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil.'

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Behold — he has become like one of us. Now he might reach out and take also from the tree of life, and live forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the Lord drove out the man — to bar the way to the tree of life that he might not eat and live forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And Eden faded behind them. The gates were closed. The way was barred by flaming sword.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Years passed. Cain and Abel brought offerings. God accepted Abel's — but looked with favor on Cain's sacrifice.

choices.label: Hold your ground in anger 😠
choices.note: Cain's path. The seed of the serpent grows in the heart.

choices.label: Lay down your pride ✝️
choices.note: Cain's path not taken. But grace was still offered, if only he would listen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Cain turned on his brother Abel in the field. And the blood of Abel cried out from the ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ground was cursed. The serpent was judged. The way to paradise was barred. From dust we came — and to dust we return.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But even in exile, the promise remained — the seed of the woman would one day crush the serpent's head.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The story continues west of the divide — where the seed of the woman journeys through promise and peril, toward the dawn of redemption.
